subject: Discovery recap — MedAlign infra constraints & draft mutual action plan

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@medalign.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Discovery recap — MedAlign infra constraints & draft mutual action plan

Alex — thanks again for the time today. Below is a concise recap of the discussion, the risks you called out, and the proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of customer goals
- Move inference for PHI-sensitive workflows off public hosted endpoints into a customer-controlled environment.
- Maintain sub-250ms p99 for autofill/use-case while bounding monthly token cost.
- Meet MedAlign internal compliance for KMS rotation and audit logging.

Pain points we heard
- Network egress restrictions: inbound-only access to the cluster, strict outbound egress blocked.
- Key ownership: must use MedAlign KMS (Cloud KMS / HSM) with customer-managed key policies and quarterly rotation.
- Air-gapped approval: one environment needs a one-way data diode for research sandbox.
- Ops bandwidth: small infra team (2 people) will need runbook templates and clear SSO/KD support.

Current stack (what you shared)
- On-prem VMware clusters in two datacenters (east/west).
- Internal identity: SAML 2.0 with Okta.
- KMS: Google Cloud KMS + HSM-backed keys for production secrets.

Success criteria (what counts as a win)
- Private deployment reachable only over customer network with no egress, KMS integrated, and audit logs accessible to MedAlign SIEM.
- Performance: baseline test (1k concurrent small inference requests) meets <250ms p99 within 3% of hosted latency.
- Usability: infra runbook and deployment templates so your two-person ops can deploy/upgrade in <2 days.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP) — draft attached (MAP-draft-v1.pdf)
1) Technical deep dive with Redwood SE (Dev) and MedAlign infra: week of 12/7 — owner: Vanessa / Dev — deliverable: network diagram and KMS integration plan.
2) Security questionnaire & evidence: Redwood to provide SOC2 artefacts and a pre-filled questionnaire — owner: Marissa — deliverable: security-questionnaire.xlsx by 12/6.
3) Proof-of-concept (PoC) planning: define scope (air-gapped sandbox + one production-like cluster) — owner: Alex / Vanessa — kickoff 12/14.
4) Procurement: draft terms & SOW estimate for Dedicated private deployment — owner: Procurement / Vanessa — target initial LOI by 12/21.

Immediate asks for MedAlign (what we need from you)
- Confirm whether outbound egress is fully blocked or if restricted egress via proxy is acceptable (we discussed a one-way data diode but need explicit confirmation).
- Share a redacted network diagram (app -> load balancer -> firewall -> DMZ -> internal network).
- Point person for KMS provisioning and rotation policy (name + contact).

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (draft MAP), medalign-network-flows.png (sketch from call), security-questionnaire.xlsx (initial).

Next steps I will take this week
- Marissa will send the pre-filled security questionnaire by Monday 12/6.
- Dev will prepare a short checklist of required network ports and expected traffic flows for an air-gapped option.
- I’ll schedule the technical deep dive for 12/8 or 12/9 depending on your availability.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning next week.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
(415) 555-0184

Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — MedAlign infra constraints & draft mutual action plan

Thanks Vanessa — this is a great write-up and matches our notes. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Egress: production clusters have egress fully disabled by policy; we can open a restricted proxy port for outbound to specific IPs if strictly necessary, but our preference is inbound-only.
2) KMS: we will use Google Cloud KMS with an HSM policy; rotation is quarterly and managed by our security team (contact: Ian Chen, ian.chen@medalign.com).
3) Air-gap: the research sandbox must be fully isolated with a one-way export lane; we have an existing hardware diode we can place in front of the sandbox.

Can your PoC still run under strict outbound-disabled constraints, or will you need a temporary limited egress during setup? Also please send the network port checklist from Dev — we can have our infra team review it this week.

Happy to meet for the technical deep dive — Dec 8 at 10am PT works for me.

—Alex
Alex Taylor
Director, ML Platforms | MedAlign Health
alex.taylor@medalign.com

Alex — quick note from the infra side: we can support full inbound-only operation for steady-state inference by shipping a bootstrap bundle you apply behind your firewall. For initial image pull and attestation we have two options:

- Option A (preferred): temporary outbound allowlist to a small set of Redwood IPs for image bootstrap (automated and time-limited).
- Option B: medalign pulls images into an internal repo and we sign/verify locally (more manual).

I’ll attach the minimal ports doc in the follow-up and bring a checklist to the 12/8 deep dive.
